terms.grammar: religātus, past participle of religō, religāre, bind back
evidence: Ov. Ars 3.143: altera succīnctae religētur mōre Diānae
Hor. C. 4.11.5: quā crīnīs religāta fulgēs
terms.comment: A description: the poets tie the hair back (religāre) or gather it into one knot (in nōdum colligere), and we have found no ancient name for the tail of hair that hangs from the tie, nor one in Traupman or Levi–Bini. Morgan–Owens puts pony-tail beside braid under capillus pactilis, which is plaited hair: see “plait”.

terms.gloss: a knot of hair, hair gathered and tied
evidence: Ov. Met. 8.319: crīnis erat simplex, nōdum conlēctus in ūnum
Tac. Germ. 38: obliquāre crīnem nōdōque substringere
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a mode of dressing the hair, a knot”. Atalanta’s hair is gathered into one knot; the Suebi twist theirs sideways and bind it in a knot.

phrases.latin: Crīnēs tibi religābō, nē in oculōs cadant.
phrases.english: I’ll tie your hair back, so it doesn’t fall in your eyes.

phrases.latin: crīnis erat simplex, nōdum conlēctus in ūnum
phrases.english: her hair was simple, gathered into a single knot

phrases.latin: altera succīnctae religētur mōre Diānae, ut solet, attonitās cum petit illa ferās
phrases.english: let another have her hair tied back like Diana with her dress tucked up, as she is when she hunts the frightened beasts

sources: Lewis & Short: religo · Lewis & Short: nodus
